title: "I have not changed": why the tzimtzum leaves the Essence, and the light, as they were
overview:
The earlier chapters showed that everything below comes *mamash* (literally) from the Essence: the kindness of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is the essential kindness itself. Chapter 9 asks the obvious question. Below there is change, from *din* to *chesed*, a new creation every day, a prayer for "a new will". If it all comes from the Essence, how can He say "I have not changed"?

The answer is the *tzimtzum*. What comes down is a light, not a flow by cause and effect, and even the light comes through contractions, like one projector lamp behind many films. The change is only for the receivers. This is true of the encompassing light and of the inner light as well, at every step from the *Kav* to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, because the *tzimtzum* is not literal: the whole light is here, hidden. And the will "from before You" never changes either: He wants one thing, and only what it is dressed in changes. Rabbi Markel calls this the hardest chapter and the point of the whole book.

sections.title: The question: everything below comes from the Essence, and below there is change
sections.summary: If the kindness and the judgement of *Malchus* of *Asiya* are the Essence's own, and they change, and the world is made new every day, and we pray for a new will, then how can He say "I, *Havaya*, have not changed"?

phrases.he: (ט) אך הנה לכאורה אינו מובן מה שאמר אני יהו״ה לא שניתי שזה מדבר במלכות דאין סוף עצמו
הרי אם בבחינת מלכות דעשיה יש בו שינוי בין דין לחסד, שהוא בחינת התפעלות כו', מוכרח שגם במלכות דאין סוף יש שינוי זה מאחר שאמר אני אני הוא כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: So how could it be? If in *Malchus* of *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing as *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, and there's an actual change, in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there's *hispaalus* between *din* and *chesed*: if you say everything comes from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, so it had to be in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* also.

blocks.text: *Malchus* of *Asiya* is *mamash* (literally) the same as *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: "I, I am He." Yet in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there is change, *hispaalus* between *din* and *chesed*. If it all comes from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, the change must be there too.

phrases.he: וכן מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים בשווא ממש כנזכר לעיל דהיינו כאשר עולה ברצונו הפשוט שבעצמות ממש, להיות חפץ חסד, הרי חפץ חסד העצמי הזה יורד עד למטה ממש בחפץ חסד דמלכות דעשיה
וכן להיפך כפי המובן מכל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: So also the opposite meaning: in *gevura* it is also like that.

blocks.text: Likewise "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds": the *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) arising in the Essence's simple will arrives in *Malchus* of *Asiya*. **So also the opposite**, in *gevura* (might, restraint).

phrases.he: וגם הרי בכל יום מחדש מעשה בראשית למטה מטה שהוא בקדמין ובחוכמתא דבראשית ברא
עד רום המעלות בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: It comes *mamash*: we just said that it *mamash* comes from *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: אם כן יש בחינת חידוש גם בעצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: So if it comes from the *Atzmus*, and there's a change on the bottom, so there must be a change on the top.

phrases.he: ואיך אמר אני לא שניתי כלל
phrases.en: So how does it say: I totally didn't change at all?

blocks.text: Again: the daily renewal of creation comes *mamash* from the *Atzmus* (the Essence). A *chiddush* (newness) below that comes from there means a change at the top. So how does He say He did not change at all?

phrases.he: וכן אנו אומרים אתה הוא קודם שנברא העולם כו'
phrases.en: We also say, you're the same before the world, and you're the same after the world.

phrases.he: וכמו כן קודם שהאציל כו' וכידוע
phrases.en: Same thing: it's before it was created, it's also before it was *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: We say You are the same before the world and after it. But the world's coming was a change, and it came from Him, so He must at least have thought of changes. So too before *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל מאדם התחתון,
הרי יש שינוי גם ברצון העצמי מרצון של דין לרצון של חסד וכידוע
phrases.en: So there is, even in the *ratzon ha'atzmi*, a change in the actual *ratzon ha'atzmi*.

phrases.he: ואיך אנו אומרים
phrases.en: Also, how do we say

phrases.he: יהי רצון מלפניך,
רצון חדש,
phrases.en: We're telling Him *ratzon chadash*.

phrases.he: שיתהפך רצון של דין לחסד כו'
ואנו רואין שנויים רבים בכל יום ושעה כו'
phrases.en: And we see down here all kinds of changes,

phrases.he: בכל אשר חפץ עשה תמיד בשמים ובארץ כו'.

blocks.text: In a person even the essential *ratzon* (will) changes, from *din* to *chesed*. And "May it be Your will"? **We're telling Him *ratzon chadash***, a new will, *milfanecha*, from before You: a change in the essential will.
And **we see down here all kinds of changes**: even the Torah says He created the world, then regretted it and brought the flood.

sections.title: The answer is tzimtzum: a light, not cause and effect
sections.summary: With cause and effect, a change in the effect proves a change in the cause. But what comes down is only a light, and even the light comes through *tzimtzum*, like one projector lamp behind different films. The change is in the receivers alone, and the *tzimtzum* is not literal: the whole light is still there.

phrases.he: והתירוץ לכל זה הוא ענין הצמצום כידוע
phrases.en: The explanation is *inyan* of the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: דאם היה השפע דרך עילה ועלול,
phrases.en: If it was actually in a way of a cause and effect,

phrases.he: היה נופל ענין שינוי התפעלות כו'
phrases.en: you could say that there was actually a change in the actual cause.

phrases.he: אבל מאחר שההמשכה בבחינת אור וזיו לבד,
phrases.en: It's not that there's an actual cause and effect, so you have to say that the cause changed. It's only a light.

phrases.he: וגם הוא על ידי צמצום,
phrases.en: And even that was through different *tzimtzumim*.

phrases.he: על כן אין בעצמות אלהו״ת שום שינוי כלל, גם במלכות דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: Really, even in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* there really isn't a change, meaning the light that's in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* actually didn't change.

blocks.text: **The explanation is *inyan* of the *tzimtzum***. Were it cause and effect, *ila v'alul*, a change in the effect would mean the cause changed. But what is drawn down is **only a light**.

blocks.title: The film in the projector
blocks.text: Think of how the old-time movies worked. A projector puts out light, and a film in front of it is *metzamtzem* (contracts) the light into the picture: sometimes red, sometimes green, sometimes yellow. But the light of the projector stays exactly the same. Only the *tzimtzumim* of the light change.
So the self does not change: this is not cause and effect, where something falls because I let go of it and the change is in me. It is *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: A funny movie and a scary movie
blocks.text: A funny movie one day and a scary one the next are not a funny light and a scary light: the same light, different *tzimtzumim*.

And even the light comes through different *tzimtzumim*. So there is no change in the Essence: **even in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* there really isn't a change**. The light there is the same in itself; only what reaches you changes.

phrases.he: וכך הוא עד רום המעלות
phrases.en: And this is the way it's all the way to the top,

phrases.he: ואחר הצמצום יש בחינת שינוי,
phrases.en: it's only after the *tzimtzum* there's a *shinui*,

phrases.he: וזהו מצד המקבלים לבד כידוע.
phrases.en: this is only as far as the receivers.

blocks.text: This holds all the way to the top: only **after the *tzimtzum* there's a *shinui***, and only for the receivers.

phrases.he: וביאור ענין ההפרש בין אור לשפע ידוע לכל
phrases.en: There's a difference between an *or* and a *shefa*.

blocks.text: A *shefa* is an actual thing coming out, like water. A light loses nothing from the *etzem* (the thing itself).

blocks.title: Not the sun: Moshe's light on the elders
blocks.text: Not the sun's light, which is really a *shefa*: something comes out of the sun. Rather the light of Moshe Rabbeinu on the elders: a light, and nothing was lost.

blocks.title: A dollar out of a million
blocks.text: Give a *shefa* of one dollar out of a million and I have a dollar less. A *shefa* is the *etzem* itself coming out; a light takes nothing from it.

phrases.he: ואמנם גם בבחינת אור הוצרך להיות על ידי צמצום
phrases.en: And even in the light itself it had to be *davka* through a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ועל כן צריך כל אדם לידע ענין הצמצום ולהתבונן בו
phrases.en: So that's why you have to know, and you have to be *misbonen* in the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: בכל עולם לפי ערכו
כי הוא העיקר בכלל היחוד האלה״י באין שינוי לגבי העצמות
phrases.en: This is the main thing of how the whole thing did not really change.

blocks.text: Even the light had to come *davka* through a *tzimtzum*. So every person must know the *tzimtzum* and contemplate it in each world by its level: the changes are not in the self, nor in the light, only in how much light reaches you.
For it is the main thing: **This is the main thing of how the whole thing did not really change**.

blocks.question: In a projector there really is less light after the film than before it. Is the tzimtzum not the same?
blocks.text: No. In a projector the *tzimtzum* is *kipshuto* (literal): after the film there is *mamash* less light. In the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of worlds) it is less only for the *mekablim*; the light down here is *mamash* the original light, coming down hidden, and one who knows how can expand it back.

The light that came down is the light of the Torah, which seems a book of stories and laws, like American law, Aesop's Fables or "Confucius says". But the whole light is hidden in it: He hid it from the wicked, in the Torah.

phrases.he: וכמו קמיה כחשיכה כאורה, רוחניות וגשמיות שוין,
phrases.en: Really, that's only the way we see it. But as far as the way He sees it, it's really equal.

phrases.he: עד אצילות ועשיה שוין כידוע
phrases.en: Still by Him, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing.

blocks.text: Only the way we see it differs; the way He sees it, it is equal. **Still by Him, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing**.

sections.title: Not only the encompassing light: the inner light does not change either
sections.summary: One could grant all this for the *makif*, which is the same everywhere, and still think the inner light, *memalei kol almin*, really grows less as it descends. It does not. There is as much light here as above; the receiver is adjusted not to see it, as Bilaam was.

phrases.he: הגם שזהו לגבי בחינת המקיף בלבד
phrases.en: Even though this is only in relationship to the *makif*,

phrases.he: הנקרא סובב כל עלמין בכלל ובפרט שלמעלה מהדרגת האור שבבחינת ממלא כל עלמין כידוע

blocks.text: All this is said of the *makif*, where all is the same. In *memalei kol almin* the *or pnimi* (inner light) seems to lessen as it goes down.

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בבחינת אור פנימי, בחינת ממלא בכלל ובפרט, אין שינוי כו'
phrases.en: Really, in the *or pnimi* it's really also no *shinui*.

phrases.he: ועליון ותחתון שבו שוין
phrases.en: So that the upper and the lower is really *mamash* equal, so that really there's just as much light down here as there is up there.

blocks.text: In the inner light too there is no change: **the upper and the lower is really *mamash* equal**, an infinite light down here as up there. The change is only in the *mekablim*, who do not see it. How can it be there unseen?

blocks.title: Bilaam's donkey saw the angel
blocks.text: Like the angel with Bilaam: the donkey saw it, so it was really there; had it been invisible, the donkey could not have seen it either. As the commentators explain, there was an adjustment in Bilaam's head not to see it. The change is not in the light but in the *mekabel* (the receiver).
The Alter Rebbe could *mamash* see the infinite light down here. Were it really contracted, he would see only what came through; he saw it because the whole thing came through.

blocks.title: The prophet's servant and the chariots of angels
blocks.text: He thinks it is by Yechezkel or Yeshayahu. With the king of Aram's whole army around them, the prophet's servant was scared. The prophet said: *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d), open his eyes, and he saw millions of chariots of angels all around. They were already there, or the prophet could not have seen them. And more than angels: up to the highest levels, it is all right here. Only the receiver changed, so in *memalei* too, upper and lower are equal.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני לא שניתי,
ואני הוא בחינת ממלא כידוע
phrases.en: *Ani* is *memalei*.

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב את השמים ואת הארץ אני מלא, בהשוואה אחת דווקא
מלא
phrases.en: *Malei*, it says. Doesn't say *sovev*, it says *malei*.

phrases.he: זה גם כן בבחינת אור פנימי
phrases.en: It's also talking about the *or pnimi*.

phrases.he: וכמאמר לית אתר פנוי מיניה כידוע
phrases.en: There is no place that's empty from Him,

blocks.text: The verse speaks of the inner light too: "I have not changed", and "I" is *memalei*, as "He" is *sovev*. And "I fill the heavens and the earth" says *malei*, fill: the inner light, from which no place is empty.

phrases.he: והיינו משום דגם בבחינת ממלא בא ירידת האור והשפע על ידי צמצומים דוקא

blocks.text: Not a different light at each level: only a *tzimtzum*, and not even one in the literal sense.

sections.title: A tzimtzum at every step, from the Kav to Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: The *Kav* itself begins with the first *tzimtzum*, and every step down passes a screen that the *Malchus* above breaks through. A television is the better picture: the light behind the screen never changes and never comes through; the screen shines with a light of its own, in its own color. Inside, even Haman is a word of G-d's Name.

phrases.he: וכידוע דגם בבחינת הקו וחוט שנמשך מעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא ממלא כל עלמין דאבי''ע בכלל, הרי הוא נמשך על ידי צמצום בתחלה בעצמות והוא צמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי וחלל ריקן כו'
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: Like it explains in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: The *Kav*, the *memalei kol almin* of all the worlds, comes after the first *tzimtzum*, the *makom panui*. As Reb Hillel Paritcher said, the hollow is not a hole in the light: the light is there, you just cannot see it.

phrases.he: וכן בירידת הקו למטה בבחינת עגולים ויושר כו'
phrases.en: The same thing: how the *Kav* comes down with *igulim v'yosher*,

phrases.he: עד שנעשה בחינת כתר לאדם קדמון הוא על ידי צמצום וכן מאדם קדמון לעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין כו' וגם באצילות עצמו יש מסך בין כתר לחכמה בכלל
והוא מה שכתוב והבדילה הפרוכת פרסא בין כו'
phrases.en: In other words, it's like a film in between.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזוהר וכן מאבא ואימא לזעיר אנפין ומזעיר אנפין לנוק' כידוע

blocks.text: So it goes down level by level, through a *tzimtzum* or a screen (*masach*) at each, like the film in front of the projector that makes the shapes; the original light can make any movie.

phrases.he: וממלכות דאצילות לבריאה יש מסך, והמלכות בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר לבריאה
phrases.en: And the light goes through the *masach*, but as it goes through it gets *metzumtzam*.

blocks.text: The light goes through the *masach*, and as it goes through it becomes contracted.

blocks.title: Not a film: a television screen
blocks.text: Really it is more like a television: the light does not go through the screen. A beam hits phosphorescent bits from the inside, and a different light, an induced light, as a student puts it, shines outside. The original light is not lessened. In a color TV the beam has no colors; hitting a red piece, it produces red.

That is the better *mashal*. Through a film the light seems to change; here it does not pass through. What shines is the light of a *tolda* (a product), from the *kli* (vessel), while the original light is hidden: it hits a blue *kli* and induces the only light that *kli* can shine, blue. So *memalei kol almin* never changes.

Big and little too: fantastic light in *Atzilus*, tiny amounts in *Asiya*. But the *or pnimi*, the light of the *Kav*, is *mamash* the essential light and does not change. *Asiya* differs by its *kelim* (vessels): the light tells *chesed* of *Asiya* to act, and a tiny light of *chesed* comes out, the external light of the *tolda*. The inner light is the same all the way down, even in the *kelipos* (husks).

blocks.title: Haman and Mordechai: until one does not know
blocks.text: Yaakov and Esav, we are learning now, are brothers. Even with Haman of Amalek, worse than Esav, inside it is *ad d'lo yada*, until one does not know. Outside, Haman was the biggest *rasha* (wicked man) ever, out to kill all the Jews, and Mordechai one of the great Rebbes. Yet leave out one "Haman", like a "Mordechai", and it is not the Megillah.

blocks.title: The whole Megillah is G-d's Name
blocks.text: Outside, Haman is the *rasha*; inside is the *Aibershter*, never mentioned in the Megillah because, in short, the whole Megillah is *mamash* His Name: it is Torah, and to say the Name you read it from beginning to end. Like *Elokim*: the first three letters alone do not mean G-d, and the *hei* and *yud* alone are "Hi, hi, how you doing?" Leave out one "Haman" and it is not G-d's Name. Outside, from the *tzimtzum*, Haman is Haman; in the *or pnimi* there is no difference.

blocks.title: The beam crossing the pixels
blocks.text: The inner light tells you *Vayehi bimei Achashverosh* ("And it was in the days of Achashverosh"), like the TV's beam crossing the pixels; at Haman it says Haman, and the kids make noise. Leave it out and you have not said G-d's Name. Outside, Haman and Mordechai differ; inside, one thing tells you to say both.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יש מסך בין בריאה ליצירה ומלכות דבריאה בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר ליצירה וכן מלכות דיצירה בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר לעשיה עד מלכות דעשיה שנקרא המלך המרומם לבדו כו'

blocks.text: Why is *Malchus* of *Asiya* "the King who alone is exalted", and not *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*? It is the same King, and *davka* in *Asiya* is He so called.

In my head, in *Atzilus*, I can be a king too: "He's a legend in his own mind," which is easy. *Davka* in *Asiya* He is really the King. (In some places, though, the phrase does mean *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.)
After the tape turns over: He is King *davka* in *Asiya*, in actuality, not in His head.

sections.title: Darkness first: in the first thought there was only this world
sections.summary: "At first it arose in thought to create with judgement" means a single *tzimtzum* straight to *Asiya*. It was no mistake: this world is all He wanted, and in the first thought there is only the end. The levels in between exist for us, so that a person can climb them and reach what came before.

phrases.he: כמאמר רבותינו ז״ל כברייתו של עולם, ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא
phrases.en: First, how did He create the world? First He made dark, and then the light returned.

phrases.he: וכן משאמרו רבותינו ז''ל בתחלה עלה במחשבה לברוא במידת הדין,
phrases.en: He originally thought to make the world just with a straight *tzimtzum*, straight to *Asiya*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הצמצום דשם אלהי״ם שבמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: That's what it means, *midas hadin*: means the *bechina* of *tzimtzum* of *Shem Elokim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

blocks.text: First He made dark, then the light returned. "At first it arose in thought to create with *midas hadin* (judgement)": a straight *tzimtzum* of the Name *Elokim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, one *tzimtzum* on the light and, poof, the world. But then there would be no climbing the ladder.

blocks.question: "Then He saw that it would not work out like that." So what, He made a mistake? Oops?
blocks.text: No. He planned only this world, not *Atzilus* "and all that business". "He saw" means He always knew that for this world to work it had to go through all the *tzimtzumim*, so He joined *chesed*: the light coming through level after level.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בראשית ברא אלהי״ם,
phrases.en: So like it says, in the beginning *bara Elokim*,

phrases.he: בחוכמתא, בקדמין,
רצון וחכמה דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: Now he's telling us it's *Keser* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: וכו' וד"ל:

blocks.question: The text said earlier that "with the first" means Keser of Atzilus or higher. Now it is the Keser and chachma of Malchus of Asiya?
blocks.text: Yes: in the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought) the *Keser* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the final act, came first. The end of the deed is first in thought.

"In the beginning" depends where you look, as in the dispute whether heaven or earth came first. In actual creation the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* came first, before *Atzilus*. In the *machshava kduma*, especially the *glif glifu* (the engraving), there was no *Adam Kadmon*: straight to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. The first thing He thought of was the end.

blocks.title: The pizza
blocks.text: Wanting a pizza, you first think of having it. Getting it, you leave the house, get in the car, drive to the pizza place and all that business, and the pizza comes last; in thought it is the opposite. And the first thought is only the pizza: "the end of the deed is first in thought" does not mean the levels backwards. So all He thought of was to make the world.

blocks.question: We go through the steps because we cannot make a pizza appear; He could. And could He not have made a kind of person who could just jump, with no levels in between?
blocks.text: Of course He could have made it work. But He created the world to make known to us how things are, and He wanted a person like us who would learn *Chassidus* (the teachings of Chassidism) like this: the *seder hishtalshelus* (the order of the chain of worlds), and through it the original thing before. So He made the levels, but what He wanted was the end: "We were the intrinsic, and that whole other business is extrinsic."

blocks.title: The ground and the sun
blocks.text: He wanted people, not a ground or a sun, but to have us He needed them. Why not have us float in space? He wanted us doing mitzvos that involve the ground and the sun. What He wanted was us.

sections.title: The answer: the will "from before You" never changes
sections.summary: He wants one thing, before and after. What changes is only what that will is dressed in: candy or shouting, brown walls or pink. "May it be Your will" asks for a change in the doing, in *Asiya*, and it leans on the will that does not change. He is literally here, exactly as before the world was created.

phrases.he: ועפ"ז יתורץ הכל דמה שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי בין רצון של חסד או דין בכל עולם דאבי''ע היינו כמו שהוא קודם הצמצום ומסך שבוקע בו ונעשה כתר לעולם התחתון
ועל זה אמר יהי רצון
מלפניך דייקא
phrases.en: From You.

blocks.title: The father: candy one minute, shouting the next
blocks.text: He wants one thing, like a father who gives his kid candy one minute and shouts at him the next. What changed? "I didn't change nothing. I want my kid to succeed." If candy helps him study, candy; if shouting, shouting.

blocks.question: But in "May it be Your will" we are saying that we change the will.
blocks.text: Not even that changes the *ratzon*. The *Aibershter* wanted a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below): a house with His wife, the Jews, *Knesses Yisroel* (the community of Israel).

blocks.title: The house, the pool table and the pink walls
blocks.text:
A man builds his wife a house: brown walls, a pool table in the basement. What does she need a pool table for? She wants pink walls and a basement lounge for her friends, with hair dryers. He runs back to the architect: didn't he say he never changes, *Ani Havaya lo shanisi*? "I didn't change nothing. I always wanted to make my wife happy; brown walls or pink, I don't care."

Only the outer things the will is dressed in changed. So his wife can say *yehi ratzon milfanecha*: change this will for a pool table into a will for what she wants. So can we: He really wanted to make His wife happy.

sensitivity.reason: The analogy is built on a stock picture of what a husband wants in a house and what a wife wants (pool table against pink walls and hair dryers for her friends).

blocks.text: *Milfanecha* precisely: **from You**. The *ratzon* for what kind of wall did change, from brown to pink. But the *ratzon milfanecha*, the will from before You, is exactly the same: he wanted to keep his wife happy.

phrases.he: וכל בחינת מעלה ומטה שבעולם זה שוין כו'
phrases.en: And the whole up and down is all exactly the same as far as He's concerned.

phrases.he: אבל אחר הצמצום נמשך הרצון בחכמה ומדות בשינויים
phrases.en: Then it comes with *shinuyim*.

phrases.he: עד מלכות דעשיה, אומרים יהי רצון מלפניך, בשינוי לענין עשיה בפועל ממש, מדין לחסד וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין:

blocks.text: Up and down are the same to Him. After the *tzimtzum* the will comes **with *shinuyim***: a *ratzon* for pink walls, for green walls. The wife does not ask him to stop loving her; that will is what she plays on. She asks the *ratzon* for the *asiya*, the deed, to change.

"This is actually the hardest chapter of the whole book." Others are more intricate, but this one is the hardest to understand, and it is the point of the book: not seven and eight, with the general picture and the unifications of the *Kesarim* (crowns), *chachma* and *middos*, but this, *Ani Havaya lo shanisi*, I have not changed.

"I have not changed" is not just that the world is a garment hiding the *Aibershter*. He is literally here, as "You are He before the world was created." The *tzimtzum* changes nothing, since He is higher than spreading forth and *tzimtzum* alike; the *tzimtzum* is how He stays unchanged.

As the text explains later, the *tzimtzum* is an infinite power of the *Atzmus*; opening and closing are one power, closing almost the higher: "It's no *chachma* (wisdom) to be an infinite light in an infinite light. But to be an infinite light in a finite world is a bigger *chachma*."

blocks.title: The last of three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: Of Shlomo HaMelech's three thousand *meshalim* (analogies), the highest *chachma* is *davka* the last, putting it into so low a *mashal*. And this world is a last *mashal*.

blocks.title: What a small child thinks
blocks.text: That is the point of the whole book: the *Aibershter* is literally here, as a small child's *daas* (knowledge) has it, *mamash* standing with us, only invisible. A *maamar* (discourse) of the Mitteler Rebbe says this is so close to the truth that it is *mamash* the truth, like the angels the man could not see.

All we do and all that happens is literally the encompassing light, the inner light and the *Atzmus*, here. The *tzimtzum* makes no difference: darkness is as light, hidden the same as revealed. So this is the hardest chapter, and those that follow are its *pratim* (particulars).

Chapter nine: the ninth of Kislev is the Mitteler Rebbe's birthday and *yahrtzeit* (the anniversary of his passing). This class, on the fourth of Kislev, is in his week, building up to the ninth and tenth: a very special week.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the forms of the question the chapter opens with, and what do they share?
Why would a flow by cause and effect mean a change in the Essence, and why does a light not?
Where does the projector stop being a good picture of the *tzimtzum*, and what does the television add?
How do Bilaam's donkey and the prophet's servant show that the inner light is not lessened below?
What does "at first it arose in thought to create with the attribute of judgement" mean, if it was not a mistake?
When we say "May it be Your will", which will are we asking to change, and which will are we relying on?
